questions.question:

questions.solution:
The relationship between the first and second word is:

**Biology : Science** → Biology is a branch or subdivision of Science. Science is the broader category and Biology falls under it.

So the relationship is: **Specific Branch : Broader Category**

Applying the same logic: 

**Music : ?** → Music is a branch or subdivision of which broader category?

⇒ **Music is a branch of Art**. Art is the broader category under which Music, Painting, Dance, Theatre and other creative disciplines fall.

**Checking each option:**

 
• **"Art"** →** Correct. Just as Biology is a branch of Science, Music is a branch of Art. The broader category relationship is perfectly maintained.**
 
• "Voice" → Wrong. Voice is a **medium or tool** used in music, not the broader category that music belongs to. The pattern is not followed. 
 
• "Composer" → Wrong. A Composer is a person who creates music. It refers to a professional role, not the category that music belongs to.
 
• "Tune" **→** Wrong. Tune is a component or element of music itself, not the broader category. It is more specific than music, not broader.

 Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question:
Statement: "Bus fare will be reduced by 25% for students."

Which assumption is implicit?

options.text: Lower fares will encourage more students to travel by bus
Students can afford current fares easily

questions.solution:
Given Statement: Bus fare is being **deliberately reduced by 25%** specifically for **students** as a target group.

**Logic followed here is:**

⇒ An implicit assumption is something that is **not directly stated** but must be **believed to be true** for the statement or action to make logical sense.

⇒ A fare reduction is only a meaningful policy if the authority **believes it will bring a positive outcome** — in this case, making bus travel more accessible and attractive for students.

⇒ The action of reducing fares only makes sense if it is assumed that **cost is a barrier** and that reducing it will **encourage more students** to use buses.

**Checking each option:**

 
• "All buses are overcrowded" → False. The statement is about fare reduction for students and makes **no reference** to bus occupancy or crowding at all. This assumption is completely irrelevant to the statement.
 
• **"Lower fares will encourage more students to travel by bus"** **→ True. This is the core implicit assumption. The authority would only reduce fares if it believed doing so would make bus travel more appealing and affordable for students. Without this assumption, the policy has no logical purpose. **
 
• "Student travel is officially discouraged" → False. This directly **contradicts** the statement. Reducing fares is an act of encouragement, not discouragement. This assumption is the opposite of what the statement implies.
 
• "Students can afford current fares easily" → False. If students could already afford fares easily, there would be no logical reason to reduce them. This assumption actually works against the purpose of the policy stated.

 Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 2"**.

• "Take a photo and share online" → Completely Wrong. This is unprofessional, violates workplace privacy, could harm the co-worker's reputation unfairly, and does absolutely nothing to address the immediate safety risk.

 Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 3"**.

__
 
• **The title "Zinda Pir" or "Living Saint"** was attributed to **Aurangzeb**, the sixth Mughal emperor of India.
 
• Aurangzeb was known for his **piety and strict adherence to Islamic principles**, which earned him this title.
 
• He was highly devout and carried out his religious duties with dedication, which included performing regular prayers and fasting.

• **Aurangzeb:**

 
 
• Born on **3 November 1618**, Aurangzeb was the son of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He ruled from **1658 to 1707**, making him the longest-reigning Mughal emperor.
 
• He expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest territorial extent, covering almost the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• Aurangzeb is remembered for his **religious orthodoxy** and implementation of Islamic laws, such as the reimposition of the Jizya tax on non-Muslims.
 
• Despite his religious fervor, his policies were controversial, leading to dissent among certain communities and regions.

• **Babur:** The founder of the Mughal Empire, Babur ruled from **1526 to 1530**. He was known for his military conquests and establishing Mughal rule in India.
 
• **Jahangir:** Jahangir ruled from **1605 to 1627**. He was known for his love for art, nature, and his administrative reforms.
 
 
 
• **Religious Policies of Aurangzeb:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb's reign was marked by his strict adherence to Islamic principles, including the enforcement of Sharia law.
 
• He banned practices that he deemed un-Islamic, such as music and certain festivals, which led to criticism from various sections of society.
 
• Despite his policies, he maintained a vast and efficient administrative system that contributed to the empire's prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb's legacy remains a subject of debate among historians due to his religious orthodoxy and administrative policies.
 
• While he expanded the empire and maintained strict governance, his policies alienated certain communities, leading to resistance and eventual weakening of the Mughal Empire after his death in **1707**.

__
 
• The **Chola inscription at Uttaramerur** primarily deals with the system of **village administration**. It provides detailed insights into how the villages under the Chola dynasty were governed.
 
• The inscription, dated back to the **10th century CE**, highlights a highly organized and democratic form of governance at the village level.
 
• It describes the functioning of **local assemblies** (sabhas) and the process of electing members to these assemblies through a **lottery system**.
 
• The inscription emphasizes the qualifications required for candidates to be part of the village administration, such as **land ownership, moral integrity, and educational qualifications**.
 
• It also outlines the responsibilities and powers of these assemblies, including decisions regarding **tax collection, dispute resolution, and maintenance of public infrastructure**.
 
• This historical document showcases the advanced administrative capabilities of the **Chola Empire** and its emphasis on decentralized governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The Chola dynasty was one of the longest-ruling dynasties in Indian history, flourishing between the **9th and 13th centuries CE**.
 
• It was known for its contributions to **art, architecture, and administration**.
 
• The Cholas established a highly efficient administrative system with a strong emphasis on **local self-governance**.
 
 
 
• **Uttaramerur Inscription:**
 
 
• The Uttaramerur inscription is one of the most detailed records of village administration in ancient India.
 
• It was discovered in the temple town of **Uttaramerur** in modern-day Tamil Nadu.
 
• The inscription provides evidence of a highly democratic system where even common villagers had a say in the administration.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Village Administration:**
 
 
• Village assemblies were called **Sabhas**, and they were responsible for governing the village.
 
• Members of the sabha were chosen through a **lottery system** to ensure fairness and avoid nepotism.
 
• Sub-committees handled various aspects of governance, such as **finance, justice, and public works**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Aspects:**
 
 
• The inscription does not focus on topics like **maritime trade**, **military conquests**, or **temple rituals**, which were other significant aspects of Chola governance but are not the subject of this document.
 
• Instead, it serves as a testament to the importance of **decentralized governance** and the empowerment of local communities in the Chola Empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of the Chola Administration:**

 
 
• The Chola system of governance is often seen as a precursor to modern democratic principles, as it allowed for **elected representation** and public participation.
 
• The administrative practices documented in the Uttaramerur inscription reflect a high level of **political sophistication**.
 
• This system ensured transparency and accountability, which were crucial for the effective functioning of the empire.

• The Chola administrative system is studied worldwide for its **innovative governance** models.

questions.question: Which constitutional amendment granted constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**73rd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act**, enacted in **1992** and implemented on **24th April 1993**, gave constitutional status to **Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs)** in India.
 
• This amendment added **Part IX** to the Indian Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," which provides a framework for the structure, composition, and functioning of Panchayati Raj Institutions.
 
• It also introduced a new schedule in the Constitution – the **Eleventh Schedule**, listing **29 functional items** to be transferred to Panchayats, such as agriculture, rural development, education, and health.
 
• The amendment mandates the establishment of a **three-tier system** of Panchayati Raj governance in rural areas: **Gram Panchayat** (village level), **Panchayat Samiti** (block level), and **Zila Parishad** (district level).
 
• It provides for the **direct election** of members at all levels of Panchayats and reservation of seats for **Scheduled Castes (SCs), Scheduled Tribes (STs), and women** (33% seats).
 
• Article **243G** empowers Panchayats to function as institutions of self-government, with authority to prepare and implement plans for economic development and social justice.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Features of the 73rd Amendment:**

 
 
• **Gram Sabha:** The amendment recognizes the Gram Sabha (village assembly) as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system. It comprises all adult members in a village and acts as a decision-making body at the grassroots level.
 
• **State Election Commission:** This body is responsible for conducting elections to Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• **State Finance Commission:** The amendment mandates states to establish a Finance Commission every five years to recommend the distribution of financial resources between the state and Panchayats.
 
• **Tenure:** Panchayats have a fixed tenure of **5 years**, and elections must be held before the expiry of this period. If dissolved prematurely, elections must be conducted within **6 months**.
 
 
 
• **Other Constitutional Amendments on Local Governance:**
 
 
• The **74th Amendment Act** of 1992 provided constitutional status to **Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)** like Municipalities.
 
• The two amendments (73rd and 74th) collectively aim to strengthen grassroots democracy in rural and urban areas.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Panchayati Raj Institutions:**
 
 
• **Kerala:** Known for its exemplary decentralized governance under the Panchayati Raj system, Kerala has achieved significant progress in education, healthcare, and rural development.
 
• **Rajasthan:** The first state to implement the Panchayati Raj system in **1959** in Nagaur district.
 
 
 
• **Historical Background:**
 
 
• The concept of Panchayati Raj is rooted in India’s history and was advocated by leaders like **Mahatma Gandhi** for rural self-governance.
 
• The **Balwant Rai Mehta Committee** (1957) recommended the establishment of a three-tier Panchayati Raj system, which laid the foundation for the eventual constitutional amendment.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **42nd Amendment:** Enacted in **1976**, it is known as the "mini-Constitution" due to extensive changes in the Constitution, but it is unrelated to Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• **52nd Amendment:** Introduced in **1985**, it dealt with the anti-defection law, providing provisions for disqualification of members on grounds of defection.
 
• **99th Amendment:** Passed in **2014**, it established the **National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC)**, later struck down by the Supreme Court as unconstitutional.

• It is a unique blend of **Gothic, Mughal, and Hindu architectural features**, reflecting a fusion of Indian and European elements.
 
• The style was promoted by the British as a way to integrate elements of Indian architecture into colonial projects, while also showcasing their imperial dominance.

• This architectural movement focused on reviving traditional Dravidian architectural styles of South India.

• **Mughal-Gothic:**
 
 
• This term is often incorrectly used to describe the Indo-Saracenic style, but it is not a formally recognized architectural style.

Which of the following statements about traditional and semi-classical Indian music forms are correct?

1) Kajri is sung by women in Uttar Pradesh during the monsoon, often with night-long group dancing.

2) Qawwali, introduced by Turkish Sufis, is performed only as solo singing without chorus.

3) Tappa from Punjab features rapid, jumpy notes inspired by camel riders' songs.

4) Amir Khusro helped shape Qawwali in India as a Sufi devotional form.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 1, 3, and 4 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kajri** is a traditional monsoon song form from **Uttar Pradesh**, sung predominantly by women during the rainy season. It involves group performances, sometimes with night-long dancing. ***Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Qawwali**, introduced in India by **Turkish Sufis**, is a form of Sufi devotional music. However, it is performed with a chorus (not as solo singing). This includes a lead singer and accompanying group members. ***Statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Tappa**, a semi-classical music form originating from **Punjab**, is characterized by rapid, jumpy notes. It evolved from camel riders' songs and is notable for its intricate rhythm and expressive style. ***Statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Amir Khusro**, a revered figure in Indian classical music and Sufi tradition, played a pivotal role in shaping **Qawwali** as a devotional form in India. His contributions laid the foundation for this genre. ***Statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Thus, only statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kajri:**

 
 
• It is a seasonal folk song originating from **eastern Uttar Pradesh** and parts of **Bihar**.
 
• It is associated with the monsoon season and often depicts themes of love, longing, and separation.
 
• Kajri is popular in regions such as **Varanasi, Mirzapur, and Allahabad**.
 
 
 
• **Qawwali:**
 
 
• Qawwali is a form of Sufi devotional music that originated in the **13th century**.
 
• It is performed in a group, with a lead singer, chorus, and instrumentalists (often using harmonium and tabla).
 
• The lyrics of Qawwalis are deeply spiritual, often praising God or expressing mystical experiences.
 
• Qawwali is popular in **India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh**.
 
 
 
• **Tappa:**
 
 
• The Tappa style was developed in **Punjab** and is known for its swift, intricate, and dynamic musical notes.
 
• It was brought to the forefront of Indian classical music by **Ghulam Nabi Shori**, also known as Shori Mian.
 
• Tappa is sung in languages like Punjabi and Brajbhasha, with themes often revolving around romance.
 
 
 
• **Amir Khusro:**
 
 
• He was a 13th-century poet, musician, and scholar in the court of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Khusro is credited with the invention of several musical forms, including **Qawwali** and **Tarana**.
 
• He also introduced Persian and Arabic elements into Indian classical music.
 
• His contributions to Indian music remain influential, particularly in the realms of Sufi traditions and semi-classical music.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Folk forms like Kajri and classical forms like Tappa highlight the versatility and richness of Indian music.
 
• Sufi music, as exemplified by Qawwali, bridges the gap between spirituality and art, emphasizing the universal messages of love and devotion.

questions.question: In 1916, two major political groups in India came together to present a united front to the British. Which organizations signed this historic agreement, known as the Lucknow Pact?

options.text: Indian National Congress and Swaraj Party
All-India Muslim League and Khilafat Committee
Indian National Congress and Muslim League
Hindu Mahasabha and Indian National Congress

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian National Congress and Muslim League**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1916**, the **Indian National Congress (INC)** and the **All-India Muslim League** signed an agreement called the **Lucknow Pact**. This was a historic moment in India's freedom struggle.
 
• The pact marked the **first time that Hindus and Muslims came together on a common political platform** to negotiate with the British for greater autonomy in India.
 
• The agreement was a result of efforts by **Bal Gangadhar Tilak** from the Congress and **Mohammed Ali Jinnah** from the Muslim League. It showed their commitment to a joint political struggle against colonial rule.
 
• Under the Lucknow Pact, both parties agreed to **separate electorates for Muslims** and pledged to work together for **self-governance in India**.
 
• The pact also demanded the introduction of **greater Indian representation in legislative councils**, as well as reforms to make these councils more effective in governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of the Lucknow Pact:**

 
 
• The INC and the Muslim League were initially at odds, with the League primarily representing Muslim interests and the Congress focusing on broader national issues.
 
• The partition of Bengal in **1905** by the British caused communal divides, but the growing discontent with British policies eventually brought the two groups closer together.
 
• The failure of earlier reform initiatives, such as the **Morley-Minto reforms of 1909**, also contributed to the demand for stronger political representation and unity between communities.
 
 
 
• **Main Provisions of the Lucknow Pact:**
 
 
• **Separate electorates:** Muslims were granted separate electorates to ensure adequate representation in legislative councils.
 
• **Proportional Representation:** Representation in provincial councils would be based on the population of communities.
 
• **Self-governance:** Both parties demanded more autonomy for Indians, with a focus on self-rule under the British framework.
 
• **Religious Freedom:** Protection of minority rights and religious freedom was ensured as a cornerstone of the pact.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Lucknow Pact:**
 
 
• The pact symbolized the first significant step towards Hindu-Muslim unity in India's freedom movement.
 
• It strengthened the political movement against British rule by creating a unified front.
 
• The pact laid the foundation for future demands, such as those included in the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms of 1919**.
 
 
 
• **Important Figures:**
 
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** A prominent leader of the Congress who played a crucial role in bringing the INC and Muslim League together.
 
• **Mohammed Ali Jinnah:** Represented the Muslim League and later became a key figure in India's partition.
 
• **Annie Besant:** Active in the Home Rule League, she supported the idea of Hindu-Muslim unity during this period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hindu-Muslim Unity:** The Lucknow Pact showcased the possibility of unity between Hindus and Muslims, which was significant for India's independence movement.
 
• **Impact on British Policy:** The unified demands put pressure on the British government to introduce more reforms, although they were still limited in scope.
 
• **Criticism:** Some historians argue that the pact sowed the seeds for future communal divisions by institutionalizing separate electorates, which later became a contentious issue during India's partition.

questions.question: The Himachal range includes famous hill stations and valleys such as:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kullu, Kangra, and Kashmir**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Himachal range** is a part of the greater Himalayan mountain system and includes some of the most picturesque and popular hill stations and valleys in northern India.
 
• **Kullu**: Known as the "Valley of Gods," it is famous for its scenic beauty, temples, and vibrant Dussehra festival. It serves as a gateway to other popular destinations like Manali and Lahaul-Spiti.
 
• **Kangra**: This valley is noted for its lush green landscapes, tea gardens, and historical sites such as the Kangra Fort. Dharamshala, located in Kangra, is the residence of the Dalai Lama and a hub for Tibetan culture.
 
• **Kashmir**: Often referred to as "Paradise on Earth," Kashmir is renowned for its breathtaking landscapes, Dal Lake, Mughal gardens, and houseboats. It lies in the northernmost part of India and forms part of the extended Himalayan range.
 
• These regions collectively highlight the rich natural and cultural heritage of the Himachal and Himalayan ranges. This makes them significant not only for tourism but also for their ecological and cultural importance.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is Kullu, Kangra, and Kashmir.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Munnar and Nilgiris:**

 
 
• Munnar is a hill station in Kerala, located in the Western Ghats. It is famous for tea plantations, wildlife sanctuaries, and Eravikulam National Park.
 
• The Nilgiris ("Blue Mountains") is a mountain range in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, known for its biodiversity and hill stations like Ooty and Coonoor.
 
• These locations are part of the Western Ghats and not the Himachal range.
 
 
 
• **Ladakh and Nubra:**
 
 
• Ladakh is a cold desert region in the northernmost part of India, known for its high-altitude landscapes, monasteries, and Pangong Lake.
 
• The Nubra Valley, located in Ladakh, is famous for its sand dunes, double-humped Bactrian camels, and proximity to the Siachen Glacier.
 
• While Ladakh and Nubra are part of the Trans-Himalayan region, they do not fall under the Himachal range.
 
 
 
• **Darjeeling and Siliguri:**
 
 
• Darjeeling is a hill station in West Bengal, renowned for its tea industry, the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway (a UNESCO World Heritage Site), and stunning views of Kanchenjunga.
 
• Siliguri, also in West Bengal, acts as a gateway to Darjeeling, Sikkim, and Bhutan. It is situated in the foothills of the Eastern Himalayas.
 
• These areas are part of the Eastern Himalayan region, not the Himachal range.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Himalayan Ranges:** The Himalayan mountain system is divided into three main ranges: the Outer Himalayas (Shivaliks), the Lesser Himalayas (Himachal range), and the Greater Himalayas (Himadri).
 
• **Himachal Range:** This range is primarily characterized by lush green valleys, dense forests, and popular hill stations. It lies between the Shivaliks and the Himadri.
 
• **Tourism and Economy:** The Himachal range contributes significantly to India's tourism industry, with popular destinations like Shimla, Manali, and Dharamshala attracting millions of visitors annually.
 
• **Ecological Significance:** The region is home to diverse flora and fauna, including protected areas like the Great Himalayan National Park and Pin Valley National Park.
 
• **Geological Importance:** The Himachal range is part of the tectonic collision zone between the Indian Plate and the Eurasian Plate, making it a region of significant geological activity.

• **Shri Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai** has been appointed as the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** with effect from **May 14, 2025**. He is set to be the **53rd Chief Justice of India**.

__
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India (CJI):**

 
 
• The **CJI** is the head of the **judiciary system of India** and the **Supreme Court**, which is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• The CJI plays a pivotal role in ensuring the independence and integrity of the judiciary.
 
• The CJI is also responsible for the allocation of cases and appointment of constitutional benches to deal with significant legal issues.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• The appointment of the CJI is based on the convention of seniority, where the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as the CJI.
 
• The **President of India** appoints the CJI under Article 124(2) of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The recommendation for appointment is made by the outgoing CJI.
 
 
 
• **Notable Judgments by Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai:**
 
 
• Justice Gavai has delivered judgments on various key issues, including constitutional law, human rights, and environmental law.
 
• He has contributed significantly to cases relating to **administrative law** and **judicial review** of executive actions.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts About the Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India was established on **January 28, 1950**, after the adoption of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Supreme Court comprises the **CJI** and a maximum of **34 judges** (as per the current sanctioned strength).
 
• It functions as the **guardian of the Constitution** and is vested with the power of **judicial review**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The tenure of a Chief Justice of India is not fixed but depends on the retirement age of **65 years**, as prescribed under the Constitution.
 
• Justice Gavai will hold office as the CJI for a short period, as his retirement is due on **November 24, 2025**.
 
• The Supreme Court plays a crucial role in maintaining the balance of power between the legislature, executive, and judiciary, as enshrined in the Constitution of India.

• **Reason (R):** The statement claiming that the Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia Hills are part of the **Chotanagpur Plateau**, separated by a geological fault, is **false**. These hills are not part of the Chotanagpur Plateau but are an independent geological formation in the northeastern region of India.
 
• The Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia Hills are distinct from the Chotanagpur Plateau, which is located in central and eastern India (primarily in Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal).
 
• The **Chotanagpur Plateau** is separated from the northeastern region by vast plains and river systems such as the Ganges and Brahmaputra, and there is no direct geological fault connecting these two regions.

__
 
• **Deccan Plateau:**

 
 
• The **Deccan Plateau** is a large plateau in western and southern India, covering a substantial part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It is characterized by its ancient volcanic rocks, rich mineral resources, and distinctive topography, which includes hill ranges, valleys, and fertile plains.
 
• The northeastern extension of the Deccan Plateau includes regions such as the Rajmahal Hills and the Meghalaya Plateau.
 
 
 
• **Garo, Khasi, and Jaintia Hills:**
 
 
• These hills are part of the **Meghalaya Plateau**, which is an extension of the Peninsular Plateau region.
 
• The Garo Hills are located in the western part of Meghalaya, the Khasi Hills in the central region, and the Jaintia Hills in the eastern part.
 
• These hills are rich in biodiversity and are home to a variety of flora and fauna, as well as indigenous tribes such as the Garos, Khasis, and Jaintias.
 
 
 
• **Chotanagpur Plateau:**
 
 
• The **Chotanagpur Plateau** is located in eastern India, primarily in the states of Jharkhand, Odisha, and West Bengal.
 
• It is known for its rich deposits of minerals such as coal, iron ore, and bauxite, making it a crucial region for mining and industrial activities.
 
• The plateau is drained by rivers such as the Damodar, Subarnarekha, and Koel.
 
 
 
• **Geological Faults:**

questions.question: Which of the following biomolecules is most abundant in plant cell walls?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cellulose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cellulose** is the primary structural component of the plant cell wall and is the most abundant organic polymer on Earth. It provides strength and rigidity to plant cells.
 
• Cellulose is a **polysaccharide** composed of β-glucose molecules linked by β-1,4-glycosidic bonds. This unique arrangement allows the formation of strong microfibrils.
 
• Plant cell walls are primarily composed of **cellulose (40%-50%)**, along with other components like hemicellulose, pectin, and lignin. Hence, it is the most abundant biomolecule in plant cell walls.
 
• Cellulose molecules aggregate to form microfibrils, which are embedded in a matrix of hemicellulose and pectin, providing structural integrity to the plant cell wall.
 
• Cellulose is indigestible by humans but can be broken down by certain herbivores and microorganisms due to the presence of cellulase enzymes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Pectin:**

 
 
• Pectin is a polysaccharide found in the middle lamella of plant cell walls and helps in cell adhesion.
 
• It is water-soluble and forms a gel-like matrix, contributing to the plant's flexibility and hydration.
 
• Pectin is used in the food industry, especially in making jams and jellies, due to its gelling properties.
 
 
 
• **Lignin:**
 
 
• Lignin is a complex polymer primarily found in the secondary cell walls of plants, providing rigidity and resistance to microbial attack.
 
• It is especially abundant in woody plants and contributes to their mechanical strength and waterproofing.
 
• Lignin is not a carbohydrate but a phenolic compound.
 
 
 
• **Hemicellulose:**
 
 
• Hemicellulose is a heterogeneous group of polysaccharides present in the plant cell wall matrix.
 
• Unlike cellulose, hemicellulose has a branched structure and is less crystalline and weaker.
 
• It acts as a filler material, binding with cellulose microfibrils and providing support to the plant cell wall.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Cellulose:**
 
 
• It is used in various industries, such as paper production, textiles (cotton is primarily cellulose), and biofuel production.
 
• Cellulose is an essential source of dietary fiber, aiding in digestion and maintaining gut health in humans.
 
• In biotechnology, cellulose is often used for producing cellophane, rayon, and other biodegradable materials.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Plant Cell Wall Composition:** The plant cell wall is made up of three layers – the middle lamella, primary wall, and secondary wall. Cellulose is primarily found in the primary and secondary walls.
 
• **Role of Cellulose in Bioeconomy:** Cellulose is considered a renewable resource and plays a critical role in the development of sustainable materials and biofuels.
 
• **Enzymatic Degradation:** Cellulase enzymes produced by fungi, bacteria, and some animals (e.g., termites) are responsible for breaking down cellulose into glucose.
 
• **Global Abundance:** It is estimated that plants produce about **100 billion tons of cellulose annually**, making it the most abundant biopolymer in the biosphere.

questions.question:
The Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita(BNSS) allows for trials to proceed in the absence of the accused in certain circumstances.

This provision applies specifically to:

options.text: Any accused person who fails to appear.
Accused persons who are gravely ill.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Proclaimed offenders who abscond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS)** introduces provisions allowing trials to proceed in the absence of the accused under specific circumstances.
 
• This provision is applicable mainly to **proclaimed offenders**, which refers to individuals who have been declared absconders by the court due to their deliberate evasion of legal proceedings.
 
• Under the BNSS, a person can be tried in absentia if they are classified as a **proclaimed offender** as per the procedure outlined in the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC).
 
• The term "proclaimed offender" under the CrPC is applied when an individual fails to appear before the court despite repeated summons and public notifications, often under **Section 82 of the CrPC**.
 
• Such provisions ensure that justice is not delayed or obstructed due to the deliberate actions of absconding accused individuals. ***Hence, option 3 is correct.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS):**

 
 
• The BNSS is a new codification that consolidates existing laws related to criminal justice administration, including aspects from the **Indian Penal Code (IPC), Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), and Evidence Act**.
 
• The legislation aims to modernize India's criminal justice system by introducing reforms such as **speedy trials, digitization, and victim-centric approaches**.
 
• Key features include provisions for electronic evidence, improved mechanisms for witness protection, and enhanced accountability of law enforcement agencies.
 
 
 
• **Proclaimed Offender under CrPC:**
 
 
• A proclaimed offender is declared under **Section 82 of the CrPC**, where the court issues a public notice requiring the accused to appear within a specific timeframe.
 
• If the accused fails to comply, they are deemed absconding and are liable for additional legal consequences, such as property attachment under Section 83 of CrPC.
 
• The process ensures that legal proceedings can advance despite the absence of the accused.
 
 
 
• **Trials in Absentia:**
 
 
• Trials in absentia are conducted when an accused deliberately avoids appearing before the court, hampering justice.
 
• Such trials are subject to procedural safeguards to ensure fairness and legality while ensuring the accused's deliberate evasion does not obstruct justice.
 
 
 
• **Other Circumstances for Non-Appearance:**
 
 
• Although BNSS focuses on absconders, other situations like illness or foreign residency may require separate legal provisions, but these do not fall under the proclaimed offender category.
 
• Specific guidelines in legal codes determine how trials proceed in such exceptional cases.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Proclaimed Offender Declaration:**

 
 
• Declared under **Section 82** of the CrPC for individuals evading legal summons.
 
• Public notice is issued, and legal proceedings can continue without the accused's presence.
 
 
 
• **Legal Safeguards:**
 
 
• Procedural fairness ensures that the rights of the absconder are protected, with legal remedies available for wrongful declaration.
 
• The court follows a stringent process before declaring someone a proclaimed offender.
 
 
 
• **BNSS Innovations:**
 
 
• Introduces streamlined processes for trials, ensuring both efficiency and justice.
 
• Focuses on reducing delays and improving accountability in criminal proceedings.

questions.question: What is the maximum period of imprisonment that can be given in a summary trial under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, irrespective of the punishment specified for the offence?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**3 months**__.
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**
 

__ 
 
• The **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023**, governs summary trials, which are trials conducted for minor offences to ensure speedy justice. 
 
• Under the BNSS, 2023, the **maximum period of imprisonment** that can be awarded in a summary trial is limited to **3 months**, irrespective of the punishment prescribed for the specific offence under general law. 
 
• Summary trials are conducted for offences that are less serious in nature, ensuring that the judicial process is expedited without compromising fairness and legality. 
 
• As per the BNSS, the purpose of restricting the imprisonment to 3 months is to **avoid excessive punishment** for minor offences and to streamline the judicial process for such cases. 
 
• This provision helps in reducing the burden on courts and ensures that resources are efficiently utilized for more severe cases. 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 

__ 
 
• **Summary Trial:** 
 
• A summary trial refers to a judicial process where cases are disposed of quickly, focusing on minor offences with simplified procedures. 
 
• It is generally used for offences that do not require detailed investigation or extended court proceedings. 
 
• Examples of offences tried under summary trials include minor theft, public nuisance, and traffic violations. 
 
 

 
• **Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023:** 
 
• The BNSS, 2023, is a revised and comprehensive code introduced to replace the Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC) in India. 
 
• It aims to modernize and streamline the judicial system while ensuring the protection of citizens' rights. 
 
• The code incorporates provisions to ensure faster disposal of cases, improved victim rights, and effective law enforcement mechanisms. 
 
 

 
• **Offences Eligible for Summary Trial:** 
 
• Offences punishable by imprisonment of less than 2 years are typically eligible for summary trials. 
 
• Examples include petty theft, public disturbances, and non-serious traffic violations. 
 
• The discretion to try an offence summarily lies with the magistrate, depending on the nature and circumstances of the case. 
 
 

 
• **Benefits of Summary Trials:** 
 
• They reduce the judicial backlog by disposing of minor cases quickly. 
 
• They ensure that individuals accused of minor offences do not face prolonged legal battles or undue harassment. 
 
• They allow courts to focus their resources on more serious and complex cases. 
 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 

 
 
• **Comparison with CrPC:** 
 
• Under the earlier Criminal Procedure Code (CrPC), summary trials also had a maximum imprisonment limit of 3 months for minor offences. 
 
• The BNSS, 2023, continues this provision to maintain consistency in handling minor cases. 
 
 

 
• **Judicial Oversight:** 
 
• Even in summary trials, the judiciary ensures that procedural fairness and justice are maintained. 
 
• Accused persons have the right to present their case, call witnesses, and cross-examine prosecution witnesses. 
 
 

 
• **Exception to Maximum Limit:** 
 
• For certain offences, if the law prescribes lesser punishment than 3 months, the magistrate cannot exceed that limit during sentencing. 
 
• This ensures adherence to the principles of proportionality in punishment.

questions.question: e-NAM is primarily aimed at which of the following?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **e-NAM** stands for **National Agriculture Market**, which is a pan-India electronic trading portal to connect existing Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
 
• The primary objective of e-NAM is to establish a **National digital market** for agricultural produce, enabling farmers to sell their produce across the nation and not be restricted to local markets.
 
• e-NAM integrates markets through a virtual platform, reducing intermediation costs, ensuring better price discovery, and improving market transparency.
 
• Launched by the Government of India on **14th April 2016**, it aims to provide remunerative prices to farmers by improving their bargaining power.
 
• As of **October 2023**, over **1000 APMC mandis** from various states and union territories have been integrated with the e-NAM platform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions and Features of e-NAM:**

 
 
• It facilitates **online trading** of agricultural commodities and integrates APMC markets across the country.
 
• Provides a single window service for all APMC-related information and services, including commodity arrivals, quality assessment, and real-time price discovery.
 
• Farmers can directly connect with buyers, avoiding intermediaries, and ensuring better returns.
 
• It supports various languages and is accessible through mobile and desktop platforms, making it user-friendly for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of e-NAM:**
 
 
• Enhances **price discovery** through a transparent auction mechanism based on the quality of produce.
 
• Reduces transaction costs and eliminates the need for physical presence at the market by allowing e-bidding.
 
• Promotes **uniformity** in agricultural marketing by streamlining processes and removing information asymmetry between buyers and sellers.
 
• Encourages interstate trade of agricultural produce, leading to better market integration at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Other Agricultural Initiatives by the Indian Government:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):** Launched in 2016, it provides a comprehensive risk cover for crops, ensuring financial support to farmers in case of crop failure.
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme:** Introduced in 2015, this scheme aims to provide farmers with information on soil health and recommendations for nutrient management.
 
• **Kisan Credit Card (KCC):** It provides short-term credit to farmers for agricultural and allied activities at subsidized rates.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY):** Launched to improve irrigation efficiency and ensure water accessibility for every farm in India.
 
 
 
• **Important Reports:**
 
 
• According to the **Economic Survey 2020-21**, the implementation of e-NAM has significantly improved market access for farmers and reduced wastage of produce.
 
• The **World Bank Report** on agriculture highlights the role of digital platforms like e-NAM in reducing barriers to market access for small and marginal farmers.

• Under the NBS scheme, fertilizer companies are compensated to sell fertilizers to farmers at subsidized rates, ensuring affordability for farmers while promoting agricultural productivity.
 
• The scheme applies to all **phosphatic and potassic fertilizers** such as DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate), MOP (Muriate of Potash), and complex fertilizers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purpose of the NBS Scheme:**

 
 
• To encourage the balanced use of fertilizers by subsidizing nutrients rather than specific fertilizers.
 
• To ensure an adequate supply of fertilizers to farmers at reasonable prices.
 
• To reduce the financial burden on farmers and promote sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Fertilizer Subsidy Structure:**
 
 
• The subsidy is calculated based on the nutrient content of fertilizers, such as the per-kg subsidy for **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and sulfur (S).**
 
• For example, if the per-kg subsidy on nitrogen is announced as Rs. 20, then a fertilizer with 10 kg of nitrogen content will receive a subsidy of Rs. 200 per bag.
 
 
 
• **Challenges with the NBS Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme focuses on non-urea fertilizers, whereas urea continues to be heavily subsidized, leading to an imbalance in fertilizer usage.
 
• Farmers often overuse urea due to its lower cost, resulting in soil degradation and declining nutrient efficiency.
 
• The government incurs a significant financial burden annually due to the fertilizer subsidy.
 
 
 
• **Steps Taken to Improve the Scheme:**
 
 
• Promoting the use of organic fertilizers and bio-fertilizers to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers.
 
• Encouraging farmers to adopt integrated nutrient management (INM) practices to improve soil health and productivity.
 
• Digitizing the subsidy disbursement process to ensure transparency and reduce leakages.
 
 
 
• **Important Data:**
 
 
• India is the second-largest consumer of fertilizers in the world, with a significant portion of the subsidy budget allocated to the fertilizer sector.
 
• The government allocated approximately **Rs. 1.75 lakh crore** for fertilizer subsidies in the **Union Budget 2023-24**.
 
• Urea accounts for the majority of fertilizer consumption in India, followed by DAP and MOP.

questions.question: What is the impact of PSU disinvestment on the government's financial structure?

options.text: It increases the government's earnings permanently
It does not affect finances at all

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It reduces government’s financial assets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Disinvestment** refers to the process by which the government sells its equity or stake in Public Sector Undertakings (**PSUs**) to private entities or the general public. This reduces the government’s ownership in these enterprises, leading to a decrease in its financial assets.
 
• The primary goal of disinvestment is often to **raise immediate revenue** for the government to meet its fiscal deficit targets or to fund development projects.
 
• When the government sells its equity in a PSU, it is essentially converting its equity into liquid cash. While this increases **short-term earnings**, it results in the reduction of long-term financial assets (**hence, the correct answer**).
 
• PSU disinvestment does not increase liabilities. Instead, it provides financial relief in many cases, especially if the PSU has been incurring losses or is underperforming. *Hence, option 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Disinvestment does not necessarily guarantee **permanent earnings**. Once the assets are sold, the government loses ownership and the future revenue streams associated with those assets. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*
 
• Disinvestment does have a financial impact on government accounts, as it changes the composition of its assets. Therefore, it is incorrect to say that it does not affect finances at all. *Hence, option 4 is also incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Disinvestment:**

 
 
• **Raise Revenue:** Disinvestment allows the government to generate revenue for development projects, infrastructure building, or reducing fiscal deficits.
 
• **Encourage Private Participation:** It promotes greater private sector participation, making PSUs more efficient and competitive.
 
• **Reduce Government Burden:** Loss-making PSUs are a financial drain on government resources. Disinvestment helps reduce this burden.
 
• **Market Development:** Disinvestment, particularly through stock exchanges, develops the capital market in the country.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment Mechanisms:**
 
 
• **Initial Public Offering (IPO):** Selling PSU shares to the public for the first time through the stock market.
 
• **Offer for Sale (OFS):** Shares of PSUs are offloaded to institutional and retail investors via stock exchanges.
 
• **Strategic Sale:** A significant portion of a PSU’s equity is sold to a private entity, often along with management control.
 
 
 
• **Examples of PSU Disinvestment:**
 
 
• In 2020, the Indian government sold its stake in **Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL)** as part of its strategic disinvestment plan.
 
• Other notable disinvestment cases include Air India, Hindustan Zinc, and Maruti Udyog.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Economy:**
 
 
• While disinvestment provides short-term fiscal benefits, it may lead to concerns about **loss of public wealth** or strategic control in key sectors.
 
• It can also lead to better efficiency and productivity if PSUs are privatized and managed effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** Disinvestment helps the government in reducing its fiscal deficit by generating one-time revenue. For example, in the Union Budget 2021-22, the government set a **disinvestment target of ₹1.75 lakh crore.**
 
• **National Investment Fund (NIF):** Proceeds from disinvestment are often routed through the **NIF** to be utilized for capital expenditure or for funding social sector schemes.
 
• **Challenges:** Some of the challenges of disinvestment include undervaluation of assets, resistance from labor unions, and public opposition due to fears of privatization.
 
• **Government Policies:** The government has adopted a **“strategic disinvestment” policy**, focusing on minimizing its role in sectors where it is not necessary.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option:

Statement 1: A surplus on the current account indicates that the country is lending to the rest of the world.

Statement 2: A current account is said to be in balance when payments exceed receipts,

options.text: Both Statement 1 and Statement 2 are correct
Neither Statement 1 nor Statement 2 is correct

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Statement 1:** A surplus on the current account indicates that the country is lending to the rest of the world. This is **correct**.

 
 
• A current account surplus occurs when a country’s total exports of goods, services, and transfers exceed its total imports.
 
• When a country exports more than it imports, it essentially generates a net financial inflow, which can be lent to other countries or invested abroad.
 
• This situation implies that the country is a net lender to the world, as it has more income than expenditure on international trade and transfers.
 
 
 
• **Statement 2:** A current account is said to be in balance when payments exceed receipts. This is **incorrect**.
 
 
• A current account is considered balanced when the total receipts (income from exports, remittances, etc.) are equal to total payments (expenses on imports, transfers, etc.).
 
• If payments exceed receipts, it results in a current account deficit, not balance.
 
• Thus, the statement is factually incorrect as it misrepresents the concept of balance in the current account.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is that **only Statement 1 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Current Account:**

 
 
• It is a component of a country’s Balance of Payments (BoP) and records the trade of goods and services, net income from abroad, and net current transfers.
 
• A positive current account balance (surplus) signifies that a country is saving more than it is investing domestically.
 
• A negative balance (deficit) indicates that a country is a net borrower from the rest of the world.
 
 
 
• **Components of Current Account:**
 
 
• **Trade Balance:** Difference between the value of exports and imports of goods and services.
 
• **Net Primary Income:** Includes income such as interest and dividends from investments abroad.
 
• **Net Transfers:** Consists of remittances, foreign aid, and other transfers between countries.
 
 
 
• **Balance of Payments (BoP):**
 
 
• The BoP is a broader measure that includes the current account, capital account, and financial account.
 
• The BoP must always balance, meaning any deficit or surplus in the current account is offset by movements in the capital and financial accounts.
 
 
 
• **Current Account Deficit (CAD):**
 
 
• Occurs when a country imports more goods, services, and capital than it exports.
 
• Financing a CAD often involves foreign borrowing or depleting foreign reserves.
 
• Persistent CAD can signal economic challenges and lead to currency depreciation.
 
 
 
• **Current Account Surplus:**
 
 
• Occurs when a country exports more than it imports.
 
• It indicates strong export performance, often associated with competitive industries and favorable trade balances.
 
• Examples of countries with consistent current account surpluses include **Germany, China, and Japan.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Factors Affecting Current Account Balance:**

 
 
• Exchange rate fluctuations can make exports cheaper or more expensive.
 
• Economic growth and demand for imported goods.
 
• Global commodity prices, such as oil or gold.
 
• Trade policies, including tariffs and trade agreements.
 
 
 
• **Key Example:**
 
 
• India generally runs a current account deficit due to high import dependence on oil and gold.
 
• In contrast, countries like Germany and China often run current account surpluses due to strong export-driven economies.

questions.question: Which year marked the beginning of India's First Five-Year Plan?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1951**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Five-Year Plan** in India was launched in the year **1951**. It was a landmark initiative aimed at the economic development of the country post-independence.
 
• The plan was introduced by the then Prime Minister, **Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru**, and it primarily focused on **agriculture, irrigation, and energy** production.
 
• The First Five-Year Plan covered the period from **1951 to 1956**, laying the foundation for planned economic development in India.
 
• The plan was based on the **Harrod-Domar model**, which emphasized capital investment to promote growth.
 
• With a total outlay of **2,069 crore INR**, the plan allocated the majority of funds to **irrigation and agriculture (31%)**, reflecting the agrarian economy of the country during that era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the First Five-Year Plan:**

 
 
• The primary goal was to boost **agriculture production** to ensure food self-sufficiency in the country.
 
• It aimed to improve **infrastructure, including transportation, energy, and irrigation facilities**, for economic development.
 
• Emphasis was also placed on **poverty reduction** and improving living standards.
 
 
 
• **Harrod-Domar Model:**
 
 
• This economic model formed the basis of the First Five-Year Plan in India and focused on the relationship between growth, savings, and investment.
 
• It suggested that economic growth could be achieved by increasing the rate of investment and the productivity of capital.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of the First Five-Year Plan:**
 
 
• There was a significant improvement in **agricultural production**, with India achieving self-sufficiency in food grains for the first time.
 
• Major irrigation projects like the **Bhakra-Nangal Dam** and the **Hirakud Dam** were initiated.
 
• Infrastructure development and increased industrial production were notable outcomes of the plan.
 
 
 
• **Other Five-Year Plans:**
 
 
• The **Second Five-Year Plan (1956–1961)** focused on industrialization and was based on the **Mahalanobis model**.
 
• Subsequent plans targeted various aspects of development like education, health, and rural development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Five-Year Plans:**

 
 
• They were instrumental in shaping India's **economic policies** and driving growth in key sectors.
 
• Helped establish a planned and centralized approach to development under the **Planning Commission** (now replaced by the **NITI Aayog**).
 
 
 
• **Key Facts:**
 
 
• The **Planning Commission** was set up in **1950** to formulate and execute Five-Year Plans in India.
 
• The Five-Year Plans were inspired by the **Soviet Union's model** of economic planning.

__
 
• **Light industries** are those that typically require less capital investment, consume fewer raw materials, and produce smaller goods compared to heavy industries.
 
• **Knitting needles** and **electric bulbs** are examples of light industries because they involve lightweight production processes and cater to direct consumer needs. These industries do not involve extensive resource extraction or heavy machinery.
 
• Light industries focus primarily on **manufacturing goods for end consumers**, like textiles, household appliances, and electronics.
 
• Other examples of light industries include the production of **toys, garments, furniture, and paper products**.
 
• Options like "Oil and Shipbuilding" and "Sewing machines and Shipbuilding" involve heavy industry elements, as shipbuilding and oil production are associated with high resource use and industrial-scale operations.

__
 
• **Light Industries vs. Heavy Industries:**

 
 
• Light industries produce **consumer goods** and are characterized by low energy consumption and less environmental impact.
 
• Examples of heavy industries include **steel production, shipbuilding, automobile manufacturing, and oil refining**.
 
• Heavy industries deal with large-scale production and require significant capital investment and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Light Industries:**
 
 
• They are often located close to markets due to the **consumer-oriented nature** of their products.
 
• Light industries usually employ **skilled labor** and are more labor-intensive than heavy industries.
 
• Their products are typically lightweight, portable, and have a **shorter production cycle**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Light Industries:**
 
 
• Textile and garment production: Includes clothing manufacturing and knitting.
 
• Food processing: Such as baking and beverage production.
 
• Electronics: Manufacturing of items like **televisions, mobile phones, and electric bulbs**.
 
• Plastic goods: Includes toys, containers, and household items.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• Light industries contribute significantly to the **GDP of developing countries** by catering to the demand for consumer goods.
 
• They generate **employment opportunities** due to their labor-intensive nature.
 
• They are crucial for **export-oriented economic growth**, especially in sectors like textiles and electronics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Examples:**

 
 
• Countries like **China, Bangladesh, and Vietnam** are known for their strong light industrial base in textiles and electronics.
 
• Japan is a leader in producing **electronics and small machinery**, which are part of light industries.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Light industries generally have a **lower environmental footprint** compared to heavy industries.
 
• However, some light industries, such as electronics manufacturing, can contribute to **e-waste** if proper recycling measures are not implemented.

questions.question:
Convert the sentence provided below from its passive voice structure to an active voice structure:

It is presumed that the documents had been tampered with by internal staff before the audit.

options.text: Internal staff had tampered with the documents before the audit.
The audit presumed tampering by staff.
The documents were tampered with before the audit.
Presumptions were made regarding document tampering.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Active voice structure: The subject performs the action upon the object.
 
• In the given sentence, the core action is in the passive dependent clause: "the documents had been tampered with by internal staff."
 
• To convert this core idea to the active voice, the agent of the action ("internal staff") becomes the subject of the new sentence.
 
• Change the passive past perfect verb phrase "had been tampered with" to its active form: "had tampered with".
 
• The original subject of the passive clause ("the documents") now becomes the object of the active sentence.
 
• Retain the time phrase "before the audit" at the end for context.
 
• *Note:* In multiple-choice questions of this type, it is common to drop the introductory passive placeholder ("It is presumed that") to create a single, strong active sentence focusing on the primary event.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"Internal staff had tampered with the documents before the audit."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: **"The audit presumed tampering by staff." – Incorrect. This completely changes the meaning of the sentence by making "the audit" the entity doing the presuming.
 
• **Option 3: **"The documents were tampered with before the audit." – Incorrect. This sentence is still in the passive voice and completely removes the agent ("internal staff").
 
• **Option 4: **"Presumptions were made regarding document tampering." – Incorrect. This is also still in the passive voice and loses the specific details of the original sentence.
